source.title: Your First Montreal Apartment
source.description: Renting in Quebec, what can landlords do and what can you do about that rent hike or broken pipe? Can a landlord ask for a deposit at the start, and kick you out at the end? A three part series that deals with the most common situations that arise at the start, middle and end of the renting process: Starting: This Video Maintaining: https://youtu.be/A_YxgBK3oxM Ending: https://youtu.be/EzaJnEFL3tU Lease Transfer Cession de bail et sous-location Montréal (pas de chambre ou de colocation): https://www.facebook.com/groups/1499524676963883/ Logement a louer, Transfer de Bail ou Colocation: https://www.facebook.com/groups/302219440277577 Montreal Lease Transfer - Transfert de bail: https://www.facebook.com/groups/628134657378466 Help Out by sharing on Facebook/Reddit. It helps immensely! Extra Content: https://www.patreon.com/PaigeSaunders Merch: https://www.redbubble.com/people/joymonger https://twitter.com/PaigeMTL https://www.facebook.com/paigemtl https://rumble.com/user/joymonger Translation/Subtitles: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Hv-kjJVajPmpJZvPBSIPqboEslryMeiiUR-e6gm5H1E/edit?usp=sharing

editorial.why_selected: A practical guide to tenant rights for first-time renters in Montreal: rent increases, repairs, and what landlords can and can't do.
learning_outcomes: Tenant rights under Quebec's rental rules
How to respond to a rent increase or neglected repair
editorial.try_next: Look up your own province's or state's tenant board and save its contact page.
editorial.context_note: Specific to Quebec law as of 2019; rules elsewhere differ.
